# Rice Cereal

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="rice-cereal-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="rice-cereal-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="rice-cereal-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Rice Cereal in the HMI library has 875 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, Co, Zn, AsIII and AsV from 7 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Garuba OD, Anglin JC, Good S, Olufemi SE, Oyawoye OM, Sodipe A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Evaluation of Heavy Metals in Commercial Baby Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Archives of Food and Nutritional Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? <li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid and monomethylarsonic acid and others, in 875 results from 7 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Garuba OD, Anglin JC, Good S, Olufemi SE, Oyawoye OM, Sodipe A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Evaluation of Heavy Metals in Commercial Baby Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Archives of Food and Nutritional Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? <strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the rice Cereal was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Garuba OD, Anglin JC, Good S, Olufemi SE, Oyawoye OM, Sodipe A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Evaluation of Heavy Metals in Commercial Baby Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Archives of Food and Nutritional Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? A National Investigation Finds 95 Percent of Baby Foods Tested Contain Toxic Chemicals That Lower Babies&#39; IQ, Including Arsenic and Lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Healthy Babies Bright Futures</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Analytical Results for Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children - TEP (FY2009-FY2024)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Garuba OD, Anglin JC, Good S, Olufemi SE, Oyawoye OM, Sodipe A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Evaluation of Heavy Metals in Commercial Baby Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Archives of Food and Nutritional Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-rice-cereal" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-rice-cereal-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of rice cereal, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-cereal-30682ad99a40:353a4b17ac6d"><summary>HMI rice cereal Pb reference · Rice Cereal, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-cereal-30682ad99a40:353a4b17ac6d"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI rice cereal Pb reference · Rice Cereal, as sold. Rice Cereal, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. In one study, lead across 191 groups of rice Cereal ranged from 0.4 µg/kg (Dry Infant Cereals, FY2018) to 32 µg/kg (Dry Infant Cereals, FY2019); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Analytical Results for Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children - TEP (FY2009-FY2024)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>

<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed rice Cereal in the same study and group. Rice Cereal, cooked (5 city composites) had lead lower at 4.3 µg/kg, against 6.2 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (rice cereal, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 1 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 15 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for total mercury were 5,000 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Analytical Results for Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children - TEP (FY2009-FY2024)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in rice Cereal?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, Co, Zn, AsIII and AsV in rice Cereal, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Garuba OD, Anglin JC, Good S, Olufemi SE, Oyawoye OM, Sodipe A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Evaluation of Heavy Metals in Commercial Baby Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Archives of Food and Nutritional Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garuba2024-heavy-metals-commercial-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? A National Investigation Finds 95 Percent of Baby Foods Tested Contain Toxic Chemicals That Lower Babies&#39; IQ, Including Arsenic and Lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Healthy Babies Bright Futures</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Analytical Results for Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children - TEP (FY2009-FY2024)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in rice Cereal, as sold from 11 results in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians from 2 to 5.5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-rice-cereal" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-rice-cereal" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in rice Cereal?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in rice Cereal?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, rice Cereal, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (5.5 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-rice-cereal" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-rice-cereal" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in rice Cereal?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in rice Cereal?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same rice Cereal.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Rice Cereal, cooked (5 city composites) had lead lower at 4.3 µg/kg, against 6.2 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (rice cereal, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-rice-cereal-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-rice-cereal-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in rice Cereal is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in rice Cereal is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 7 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jane Houlihan, Charlotte Brody · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">What&#39;s in My Baby&#39;s Food? A National Investigation Finds 95 Percent of Baby Foods Tested Contain Toxic Chemicals That Lower Babies&#39; IQ, Including Arsenic and Lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Healthy Babies Bright Futures</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guillod-Magnin R, Brüschweiler BJ, Aubert R, Haldimann M · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species">Arsenic species in rice and rice-based products consumed by toddlers in Switzerland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A, 35(6): 1164-1178</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Guillod-Magnin et al. 2018 reported inorganic arsenic at 211 µg/kg (median) in rice Cereal, as sold from Berne area retail, Aug 2016 to Mar 2017, all samples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guillod-Magnin R, Brüschweiler BJ, Aubert R, Haldimann M · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species">Arsenic species in rice and rice-based products consumed by toddlers in Switzerland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A, 35(6): 1164-1178</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guillod-magnin2018-swiss-toddler-rice-arsenic-species">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
